categories.title: Site audit and AI-readiness checkers
categories.blurb: Point these at a website and get a list of problems. Some score AI-search readiness (can AI crawlers read you, do you have schema and llms.txt). Others are classic technical SEO crawlers.

categories.title: AI visibility and citation trackers
categories.blurb: These ask AI engines questions and record whether your brand is mentioned or cited. Most need your own API keys for the AI models. Results from AI engines change from run to run, so treat the numbers as trends.

categories.title: llms.txt and machine-readable content
categories.blurb: Tools that publish an llms.txt file or Markdown copies of your pages so AI agents can read your site more easily. llms.txt is a proposed standard. Support by AI providers varies, so do not count on it for results.

categories.title: WordPress, WooCommerce and framework plugins
categories.blurb: Drop-in plugins and packages for popular platforms.

categories.title: Agent skills and MCP servers
categories.blurb: Skills and MCP servers that let a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and similar) run SEO and AI-search work for you.

categories.title: Self-hosted SEO platforms
categories.blurb: Bigger open-source alternatives to paid SEO suites. Some cover AI search, some do not. Check what each actually ships.

categories.title: Research, playbooks and specs
categories.blurb: Reading material and research code. Good for learning what actually moves AI citations.

categories.title: Other awesome lists
categories.blurb: Related lists worth a look. This list does not try to replace them.

header:
Awesome AI Search Optimization

> Open-source GitHub repos for AI SEO, AEO and GEO: making your site visible to ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini and Google AI Overviews. AEO = Answer Engine Optimization. GEO = Generative Engine Optimization. Same idea: get your content found and cited when people ask AI instead of searching Google. **Rules of this list:** every repo exists, is public, is not archived and has a license or a clear note. Each line is written in plain words. Repos are listed on merit, including the maintainer's own (marked). Star counts are live badges. Details of how entries are checked are in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Part of a series of use-case directories of GitHub tools. Last full check: 2026-10-17.
footer:
## How to choose

- **I just want to know if my site is OK for AI search:** start with an audit tool from the first section. Run two and compare.
- **I want to know if AI actually mentions my brand:** use a tracker. Budget for API costs, and run it weekly, not once.
- **I use WordPress:** try a plugin from the plugins section, but read what it changes before you enable it.
- **I already use a coding agent:** install one skill, not five. Skills overlap a lot.
- **I run a docs site:** an llms.txt generator for your framework is a cheap, low-risk step.
- **Be careful:** many repos here are young and move fast. Check the last commit, read the open issues, and test on a staging copy before pointing any auto-fixer at a live site.

## Contributing

Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Short version: open a pull request, one repo per PR, use the template. Real repos only, written in plain words.

## About

Maintained by [@devanasolver](https://github.com/devanasolver), who also builds [AIRankWP](https://airankwp.com), a WordPress plugin for AI-search visibility. Listings are decided by the criteria in CONTRIBUTING, not by who owns the repo.
